transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Got it—so calls are getting answered during the day. What happens after hours or when she’s on another call, at lunch, or out sick?
User: Janet's been here 9 years. We just call people back. Haven't really counted any missed calls.
Agent: Makes sense—if Janet’s been steady for 9 years, that’s huge. When a call does go to voicemail and you call back later, how often do they actually pick up or text back versus you never reaching them?
User: Honestly, not sure. We never really counted misses. Feels like a solution looking for a problem.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you—if you haven’t seen it be a problem, it can feel unnecessary. What kind of business is this?
User: It's an auto body shop. We've been doing just fine with the way things are now.
Agent: Got it—auto body, and you feel good about how it’s running today. During your busiest stretch (usually mornings), if two calls hit at once or Janet’s tied up with a walk-in, what happens to the other caller?
User: We just call them back when we get the chance. It's been working fine for us so far.
Agent: Makes sense—if callbacks are working, I wouldn’t try to fix what isn’t broken. Roughly how many calls a week would you guess still end up going to voicemail, even with Janet up front?
User: Honestly, I've never really counted. A few here and there, but nothing that's seemed too problematic.
Agent: Got it—a few here and there. When you do call those people back, do you ever find they’ve already booked with another shop?
User: Sometimes, but that's just how it goes. Can't win 'em all, right?
Agent: Right—some slip through no matter what. When that does happen, is it usually higher-value jobs (insurance work/collision repairs) or more the smaller stuff?
User: It's a mix. Could be anything from a quick fix to a big insurance job. Hard to say.
Agent: Totally—it's random, which is what makes it tricky. If you could catch even the “few here and there” you miss—especially after hours—would you want that, or are you already at capacity where more jobs would be a headache?
User: We're busy, but more jobs aren't a headache. If it helps catch those we miss, I might be interested.
Agent: Got it—so if it helps you grab the ones that would otherwise drift to another shop, you’re open to it. Mind if I do a super quick 30‑second back-of-napkin calculation on what “a few here and there” could mean in dollars?
User: Alright, if you think it'll help make the case clearer, go ahead with your quick calculation.
Agent: Perfect—thank you. So ballpark, how many calls per week do you think still hit voicemail… 5, 10, 15?
User: I'd say around 15 calls a week might hit voicemail during busy hours.
Agent: Got it—15 a week. Of those, what percent do you think would’ve booked if you’d answered live—like 30%, 50%, 70%?
User: Probably about 50% would book something if we could answer them right away.
Agent: Got it—50%. And what’s your average ticket value on a booked job—are we talking more like $500, $1,000, $2,500?
User: Our average ticket value is around $1,100.
Agent: Got it—so with 15 missed calls/week, ~50% booking, and a $1,100 average ticket, that’s about **$8,250/week**, or roughly **$35,700/month** in work that can slip to the next shop when you can’t answer live.  

Cool. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough—Jay will show you exactly how it works and what your numbers look like with it on. What’s better for you—later today or tomorrow?
User: Alright, as a backup layer I can see it. Book your demo. Tomorrow works better for me.
Agent: Makes sense—tomorrow works. What’s your first name?
User: Just call me Dave. Tomorrow sounds fine, let's see what you've got.
Agent: Got it, Dave. What’s your last name?
User: Kowalski, like the shop name. But hey, just call me Dave. Looking forward to the demo.
Agent: Got it, Dave Kowalski—thanks. And which time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: Eastern Time Zone, Boston, MA.
Agent: Perfect—Eastern. And… is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: Yes, the number I called from is best. Looking forward to seeing how this might work for us.
Agent: Perfect—thanks, Dave. For tomorrow, I can get you in as soon as **1:15 PM** or **2:00 PM** Eastern; which works?
User: Let's go with 2:00 PM Eastern. That gives me enough time to wrap up the morning tasks.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: One sec—my calendar’s being a little finicky, I’m re-confirming it now.
Agent: Dave, I’m having trouble confirming the calendar on my side right now—but I’ve got **tomorrow at 2:00 PM Eastern** held, and we’ll reach you at your number within the hour to lock it in. Does that work on your end?
User: Sure thing, take your time. Looking forward to seeing what this can do for us.
Agent: Thanks, Dave! You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details—you can add it to your calendar in one click, or reschedule if you need to. Is there anything else I can help you with?
